questions.question: The angle of elevation is measured between:
options: the vertical and the line of sight
the horizontal through the eye and the line of sight tilted UP
the ground and the top of the object

questions.question: The most common depression error is:
options: measuring the angle from the vertical cliff face instead of from the horizontal — depression always hangs below the horizontal
placing the observer at the bottom

questions.question: The angle of depression from a clifftop to a car equals the angle of elevation from the car to the top because:
options: the two horizontals are parallel and the line of sight is a transversal — alternate angles are equal
elevation and depression are the same word

subtopics.title: The Three-Step Method — Sketch, Label, Choose the Ratio

questions.question: A surveyor 35 m from a mast measures elevation 28° to the top. Labelling from the 28° angle:
options: the mast is the hypotenuse and 35 m is opposite
the mast is adjacent and 35 m is opposite
both the mast and 35 m are adjacent
the mast (h) is opposite, 35 m is adjacent, and the line of sight is the hypotenuse

questions.question: With adjacent known and opposite wanted, the correct equation is:
Before computing 35 × tan 28° you must:
options: confirm the calculator is in degree mode — the little D on the screen

subtopics.title: Finding an Angle and Finding a Distance

questions.question: A 6 m ladder has its foot 1,8 m from the wall. The angle with the ground satisfies:
To recover the angle from cos θ = 0,3 you must:
options: use the inverse cosine: θ = cos⁻¹(0,3) ≈ 72,5°
look up 0,3 in a tangent table

questions.question: From a 45 m cliff the depression to a car is 32°. Using the alternate angle at the car, the distance d satisfies:
When the unknown sits in the BOTTOM of the ratio, the safe procedure is:
options: guess the operation and check by eye
write the equation first, then rearrange — here you divide by the tan, not multiply

questions.question: From P the elevation to a tower is 35°; 25 m closer at Q it is 55°. The key strategy is:
options: both triangles share the same height — write h from each and equate the expressions

questions.question: With d the distance from the NEARER point Q, the equation to solve is:
Solving gives d = 25 tan 35° ÷ (tan 55° − tan 35°) ≈ 24,05 m. The height is then:

subtopics.title: Looking Up, Looking Down — Everything Starts Level

questions.question: Every angle in this topic starts from:
options: the vertical wall of the building
the imaginary level line through your eyes

questions.question: Watching a drone climb higher above the field, your angle of elevation:
options: grows — a bigger tilt up from level as the drone moves toward overhead

questions.question: 'The angle you look down at your friend equals the angle your friend looks up at you' works because:
options: friends always stand at equal distances
your level line and the flat field are parallel, and one line of sight crosses both — alternate angles

questions.question: Standing inside the 28° angle, the three sides of the mast triangle are:
options: opposite = the mast, adjacent = the 35 m of ground, hypotenuse = the line of sight
opposite = the ground, adjacent = the mast, hypotenuse = the line of sight
opposite = the line of sight, adjacent = the mast, hypotenuse = the ground

questions.question: The pair 'opposite and adjacent' selects which ratio in SOH CAH TOA?
options: none; you need the hypotenuse first

questions.question: A 40 m zipline cable rises at 25°. The platform height uses:
options: sine, because the pair is opposite and hypotenuse: 40 × sin 25° ≈ 16,9 m

subtopics.title: Reading the Story Into a Sketch

questions.question: In any story sketch, the right angle is found:
options: where the vertical object meets the horizontal ground — the story builds it for you

questions.question: 'From the top of the cliff, the angle of depression is 32°.' The angle is sketched:
options: at the top, hanging below a small level line drawn through the observer's eye
at the car, above the ground
at the base of the cliff

questions.question: Your calculation says a communications mast is 1 860 m tall. Habit four says:
options: write it down — the calculator is never wrong
read the picture back: no mast is that tall, so check the mode and the ratio before anything else
convert it to kilometres for neatness
